name: Borgo Egnazia
insider_take: This isn't just a resort—it's a meticulously crafted Puglian village where ancient traditions meet modern luxury in Italy's stunning heel.
whats_special: Borgo Egnazia was built to replicate a traditional Apulian borgo (village) using local limestone and ancient building techniques. The resort sits between centuries-old olive groves and the crystal-clear Adriatic Sea, featuring its own private beach club and world-class Vair Spa inspired by ancient Roman wellness rituals.
pro_tip: Book the trullo-style accommodations—these iconic cone-roofed structures are UNESCO-protected architectural gems unique to Puglia, and Borgo Egnazia's versions are among the most luxurious interpretations you'll find.
dont_miss: The nearby UNESCO World Heritage trulli houses in Alberobello (30 minutes away) and the baroque masterpiece of Lecce, known as the "Florence of the South." On-property, experience the cooking school where you'll learn to make orecchiette pasta and burrata cheese with local nonnas (grandmothers).
pros: Authentic Puglian village atmosphere with traditional architecture
World-class Vair Spa with comprehensive wellness facilities
Multiple acclaimed restaurants featuring local and international cuisine
Extensive recreational amenities including golf course and beach club
cons: Remote location requires transportation for off-property exploration
